about.title: About me — Sookie / Jaesook Jeong
about.description: Jaesook Jeong, frontend and graphics engineer. A maker’s perspective on installation art, startup work and new technologies.
about.intro: I'm Jaesook Jeong, also known as Sookie. I work on frontend development and graphics.
about.backgroundIntro: I studied digital art and fine art and made installation work. As a developer, I still enjoy turning an idea into something tangible that other people can experience.
about.startupsExperience: I have spent much of my career working intensively in fast-moving startups. Short development cycles exposed me to a wide range of products and technologies, and I have enjoyed taking on unfamiliar problems.
about.curiosity: When I encounter a new technology, I wonder what I could make with it. If there is something I want to build, I am happy to learn what it takes, whatever the discipline. I enjoy trying unfamiliar tools in actual work and discovering what they can do.
about.cultures: Living in Germany for many years introduced me to different cultures and perspectives. I enjoy exchanging ideas and making things with people from different backgrounds, and I want to keep working in that kind of environment.

labFieldForm.theGraphicsExperimentBehindThisSiteS: The graphics experiment behind this site’s background.
labFieldForm.tryDifferentFormsAndRenderingPaths: Try different forms and rendering paths.
labFieldForm.frameIntervalsMeasuredInThisBrowserThese: Frame intervals measured in this browser. These are not GPU execution times or results from other devices.
labFieldForm.aGraphicsExperimentBuiltForThisPortfolio: A graphics experiment built for this portfolio. Rust, wgpu and WGSL maintain positions and velocities on the GPU; selecting a project changes the target shape. The same canvas stays in place across page transitions while the HTML content updates separately.
labFieldForm.theSilverParticlesAndSenseOfDepth: The silver particles and sense of depth draw on a Pmndrs example; the organic shapes and open space reference stills from Phantom Garden. The surface functions, motion and page transitions were implemented specifically for this site.
labFieldForm.aStableIdAndIntegerHashProvide: A stable ID and integer hash provide 2D samples and layer indices. The same sample IDs define positions across ten shapes, including ribbons, shells, knots, frames and orbits, preserving correspondence between pages.
labFieldForm.theComputeShaderReadsEachParticleS: The compute shader reads each particle’s position and velocity and applies a damped spring toward its target surface. Analytic curl fields drive both surface flow and the drifting particles around it.
labFieldForm.surfaceDeformationAndFreeDriftHaveSepara: Surface deformation and free drift have separate strengths. A stable subset of roughly 9% of particles drifts around every form at the same strength. In Repeated cells, cell centers stay fixed and the body particles rotate within each cell.
labFieldForm.aShortPointerHistorySuppliesDirectionAnd: A short pointer history supplies direction and speed for local forces. The cell array responds through particle size and brightness, while drifting particles also move under the force. Scrolling changes the view and layer spacing. A cap on the simulation time step prevents large jumps when returning to the tab.
labFieldForm.gpuStorageBuffer32BytesPerParticle: GPU storage buffer · 32 bytes per particle
labFieldForm.eachParticleUpdatesOnlyItsOwnState: Each particle updates only its own state. Since no neighboring particle state is read, this path does not need ping-pong state buffers. Rendering reads the same buffer after the compute pass completes.
labFieldForm.depthAndPerSampleSizeVariationMix: Depth and per-sample size variation mix fine points with larger bokeh. This is sprite-based depth styling, not a physical full-screen depth-of-field pass. Particle count and DPR are capped to limit the cost of overlapping translucent particles.
labFieldForm.theCanvasPersistsDuringNavigationANew: The canvas persists during navigation. A new target does not reset particle positions or velocities. The loop stops in hidden tabs, and reduced-motion preferences display the final shape without continuous animation.
labFieldForm.whenWebgpuIsUnavailableTheSiteTries: When WebGPU is unavailable, the site tries a WebGL2 vertex-morph fallback. It approximates deformation from the same input history but does not retain compute simulation state or provide velocity visualization. If both paths fail, the content remains readable with a static background.
labFieldForm.theRunningShaderRustEntryPointAnd: The WGSL shaders, Rust renderer, browser controller and build instructions are available below.
labFieldForm.rustCrateWgslBrowserCodeAndBuild: Rust crate, WGSL, browser code and build instructions

study.conceptDiagramOfReducingAMotionSequence: Concept diagram of representing FK animation with a smaller set of IK targets.
study.extractHandAndFootPositionsAndPole: Extract hand and foot positions and pole vectors from the bone hierarchy’s world transforms. The first step is to reconstruct the pose with Two-Bone IK and compare it with the original.
study.selectKeysFromTargetTrajectoriesAndUse: Select keys from target trajectories and use Lerp/Slerp interpolation as a baseline. Correction deltas would preserve rotations that IK alone cannot retain. The plan is to evaluate position and rotation error, ground contact and file size together.
study.aLaterStageWouldTestWhetherLearned: A later stage would test whether learned interpolation improves on the baseline, accounting for the cost of downloading the model and running inference.

contentPlatform.webClientDevelopmentAtBluebeakerContentS: Web client development at Bluebeaker: content search and storage, 3D viewers and editors, admin tools and asset optimization.
contentPlatform.iBuiltWebServicesForFindingEditing: I developed the web clients, 3D viewers and editors for a 3D content platform.
contentPlatform.connectingTheContentLibraryToViewersAnd: Connecting the content library to viewers and editors
contentPlatform.iDevelopedTheClientsForBluebeakerLab: I worked on the clients for Bluebeaker Lab and Medmap Library, Doctor and Showroom, implementing search, content storage, model editing, capture and downloads. The recording above shows model interaction in the 3D viewer.
contentPlatform.bluebeakerRecordingRotatingAndZoomingAFa: Bluebeaker recording: rotating and zooming a face model in the 3D viewer.
contentPlatform.inLibraryIConnectedSearchTermsContent: In Library, I connected search terms, content types, categories and pagination to API requests. I handled empty results and page changes, and deferred autocomplete requests until Korean text composition was complete.
contentPlatform.iConnectedFolderCreationRenamingAndFile: I connected folder creation, renaming and file management, then switched between model, image and video viewers according to the selected content. In the 3D viewer, UI state was wired to camera resets, viewpoint changes and capture actions.
contentPlatform.doctorRanAsAWebInterfaceInside: Doctor ran as a web interface inside a WPF application. I received content information from the host through its WebView and applied it to the viewer, connecting web editing with the surrounding GUI.
contentPlatform.iBuiltAdminScreensWhereOperatorsAnd: I built admin screens where operators and designers could register content and check its rendering. The workflow went beyond uploading a file: it included model information, thumbnails, previews and rendering settings.
contentPlatform.theClientFirstCreatedContentMetadataRequ: The client first created content metadata, requested upload URLs, and sent the files and thumbnails. Once the upload finished, it refreshed the list so the new content was visible on the same screen.
contentPlatform.iConnectedPanelsForCameraCalibrationLigh: I connected panels for camera calibration, lighting, shadows, SSS and interaction limits to the viewer. Designers could inspect a model’s appearance through controls instead of editing code.
contentPlatform.iWorkedOnBothViewerInteractionAnd: I worked on both viewer interaction and asset size. Reducing file size alone was not enough: I compared details before and after optimization with designers and agreed on suitable settings for the web.
contentPlatform.iUsedThreeMeshBvhForModel: I used three-mesh-bvh for model picking and scissor regions to render multiple views. In Lab, I kept the canvas alive across navigation and connected DOM controls to the 3D scene.
contentPlatform.withGltfTransformIRemovedDuplicateAnd: With gltf-transform, I removed duplicate and unused data and automated mesh merging and simplification. I applied Draco and Meshopt to geometry and KTX2 to textures. Changes to normal maps and important details were checked in a preview before adjusting the parameters.

realtimeGame.amosGameClientBuiltWithReactAnd: Amos game client built with React and Three.js: sign-in, real-time UI, XState state management, clip/IK animation and card rendering.
realtimeGame.iBuiltTheWebClientForA: I built the web UI and state management for a realtime game, along with its 3D dealer animation and card rendering.
realtimeGame.fullGameClientDevelopmentDevelopmentLead: Full game client development · Development lead
realtimeGame.userInputServerEventsAndUiState: User input, server events and UI state
realtimeGame.dealerAnimationWithClipsAndIkCard: Dealer animation with clips and IK; card rendering
realtimeGame.iDevelopedTheClientForAReact: Sign-in and game panels used React, while Three.js rendered the dealer and cards. Server events and game phases drove updates to both the UI and the 3D scene.
realtimeGame.amosRecordingBaccaratWebUiDealerCard: Amos recording: baccarat web UI, dealer card handling and camera changes.
realtimeGame.theClientJoinedRoomsAndReceivedGame: The client joined rooms and received game and user events through Socket.IO. I mapped events to XState transitions instead of having each screen interpret them independently, and passed changes from the previous game data to child state machines.
realtimeGame.iManagedAuthenticationSeparatelyFromTheW: I managed authentication separately from the waiting, betting, dealing and result phases. Each phase enabled the appropriate panels, timers and inputs. React components subscribed to the state they needed to display.
realtimeGame.reactHookFormManagedSignInInput: React Hook Form managed sign-in input, with field-level errors based on API responses. I also integrated localized text, mobile detection and sound settings into the client alongside the game screen.
realtimeGame.theDealerSHandsHadToMatch: The dealer’s hands had to match the card positions. Rather than add a clip for every position, I played prepared movements as animation clips and used CCDIKSolver to adjust hand positions while handling cards.
realtimeGame.clipsHandledEntryAndReturnMovementsDurin: IK positioned the hands during dealing, while animation clips handled the other movements. I skipped IK updates during clip playback so the two systems would not control the same bones at once.
realtimeGame.cardsSharedGeometryAndMaterialThroughIns: Cards shared geometry and material through InstancedMesh. Per-instance UV regions selected the right card from an atlas, allowing different cards to be drawn through one mesh structure.
realtimeGame.conceptDiagramOfCardRenderingWithShared: Card rendering with shared geometry and materials, using per-instance positions and UVs.

rustRenderer.iDesignedAndImplementedA2dVector: I designed and implemented a 2D vector renderer for use across multiple platforms.
rustRenderer.aConsistentInterpretationOfEachShape: A consistent interpretation of each shape
rustRenderer.choosingRecoveryBehaviorByFailureType: Choosing recovery behavior by failure type
rustRenderer.theProjectMovedRenderingFromProtopieS: The project moved rendering from ProtoPie’s platform-specific DOM and native views into a shared GPU engine. I designed and implemented the architecture and core rendering paths of a 2D vector renderer built with Rust and wgpu.
rustRenderer.iSeparatedResponsibilitiesForScenesRende: I separated responsibilities for scenes, render commands, geometry processing and GPU resource management, and defined rendering rules shared across platforms.
rustRenderer.interpretingStrokeWidthOrAlignmentIndepe: Interpreting stroke width or alignment independently at each stage can make calculated bounds disagree with the rendered result. I designed a shared interpretation that is computed once and reused across stages.
rustRenderer.conceptDiagramOfSharingStrokeInterpretat: Shared stroke interpretation across bounds, paint and geometry — concept diagram.
rustRenderer.iAlsoDistinguishedChangesThatRequireRebu: I also distinguished changes that require rebuilding geometry from changes, such as color, that only update paint properties. This keeps rendering consistent while avoiding unnecessary work.
rustRenderer.operationsSuchAsBlurAndCompositingConsum: Operations such as blur and compositing consume earlier results, so execution must respect dependencies between passes. I designed the render graph to determine pass order and manage when temporary textures holding intermediate results are needed.
rustRenderer.conceptDiagramOfPassDependenciesAndTempo: Concept diagram of pass dependencies and temporary texture lifetimes.
rustRenderer.planningAndGpuCommandEncodingWereSeparat: Planning and GPU command encoding were separate stages, allowing graph construction and backend implementation to be developed independently.
rustRenderer.applyingOneRetryPolicyToTransientFailure: Applying one retry policy to transient failures and invalid input can repeat work that will never succeed. I distinguished between reconfiguring the render target, retrying on a later frame and waiting for new input according to the cause.
rustRenderer.transientFailuresRetryOnALaterFrame: Transient failures retry on a later frame. If the render target changed, it is reconfigured first.
rustRenderer.workThatConsistentlyFailsOnTheSame: Work that consistently fails on the same input is retried only when that input changes.

webPlatforms.iBuiltTheKoreanAndEnglishSites: I built the Korean and English sites with Next.js. On each homepage request, the server fetched posts and banners and passed them to the page. User-facing features were connected according to membership status.
webPlatforms.theClientSPaymentCompleteResponseWas: The client’s payment-complete response was not used directly to update membership. The server queried the payment provider again, checked the order amount and payment status, and only then updated payment and membership-tier information.
webPlatforms.theAdminInterfaceManagedMembersDuesBoard: The admin interface managed members, dues, boards and events, as well as desktop/mobile banner images and their order. I integrated Tiptap for formatting, links and image uploads, and connected the analytics screens to Google Analytics Data API results.
webPlatforms.iDevelopedEncSPublicWebsiteAnd: I developed ENC’s public website and admin CMS. Alongside practice-area and insight pages, I built the screens for replacing banners and editing articles. The CMS fields matched the public page structure, with API integration carrying edits through to the website.
webPlatforms.reproductionOfEncSOriginalResponsiveHome: ENC website homepage with its main banner and navigation
webPlatforms.encSOriginalCmsForDesktopMobile: ENC CMS controls for desktop and mobile banners and display order
webPlatforms.pagesUsedSharedNextJsAppRouter: Pages used shared Next.js App Router layouts and practice-area templates. Query parameters selected sections within practice areas, while insight pages connected API-loaded content with previous and next articles.
webPlatforms.eachBannerHadSeparateDesktopAndMobile: Each banner had separate desktop and mobile images, a link and a display order. Drag-and-drop changes were saved, then query data was refreshed so the admin UI showed the stored result.
webPlatforms.iCustomizedTiptapSImageExtensionTo: I customized Tiptap’s image extension to persist size and alignment, and implemented drag-to-resize behavior in a React NodeView. The create and edit screens sent the resulting HTML and attachment data to the API.

xr.iDecomposedTheEstimatedPoseMatrixInto: I extracted rotation and position from the pose matrix returned by AlvaAR, converted the axis directions, and updated the Three.js camera’s quaternion and position. Updates only used available poses; detected plane poses were stored separately from camera poses.

trackingFigure.description: Camera frames are cropped to the viewport and passed as ImageData to AlvaAR. AlvaAR estimates a camera pose matrix. Rotation and position are extracted, axis directions are converted, and the result is applied to the Three.js camera.
trackingFigure.caption: The viewer prepares frames and converts poses. AlvaAR estimates the camera’s position and orientation.
